q: Which figure is used to start or stop fluid flow in a major water line?
n: Figure C is used to start and stop flow in a major water line. Shut-off valves like this are installed on mains to isolate sections for maintenance. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (valves).

q: Which figure is also known as a sluice valve?
n: A gate valve, also called a sluice valve, raises or lowers a flat gate across the flow. Figure A shows it. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; ASME B16.34.

q: Which figure features a spherical closure element and typically has a handle that does NOT rotate more than 90 degrees?
n: A ball valve has a spherical closure with a bore and opens and closes with a quarter turn (90°). Figure D shows it. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; MSS SP-110.

q: Which figure is commonly used to connect to a water closet?
n: An angle valve (Figure D) is the supply stop that connects to the water closet tank. Source: Plumbing fixture installation practice; ASME A112.18.1.

q: Which figure represents a one-way valve?
n: A check valve (Figure E, swing type) lets water flow one way only and closes against reverse flow. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; MSS SP-71.

q: What jointing method is commonly used for HDPE pipes?
n: HDPE cannot be solvent-welded, so it is joined by heat fusion: electrofusion couplers or butt fusion. Source: ASTM F2620 (heat fusion of PE pipe); ASTM F1055.

q: HDPE stands for:
n: HDPE = high-density polyethylene. HDPE pipes are tough, flexible and corrosion-resistant, so they are widely used for water supply and drainage lines. Source: ASTM D3350 (PE plastics).

q: What is the typical design life of HDPE pipe?
n: HDPE pressure pipe is designed for at least 50 years of service, with life often quoted up to 100 years. Source: Plastics Pipe Institute (PPI) Handbook of PE Pipe.

q: Which statement about HDPE pipe is NOT true?
n: HDPE has a smooth bore with low friction, so it has good flow capacity. The other statements (chemical, soil-movement and impact resistance) are true. Source: PPI Handbook of PE Pipe.

q: What is the standard color of HDPE plumbing pipes?
n: HDPE water pipe is typically black, stabilized with carbon black against UV, often with blue stripes for potable water. Source: PPI Handbook of PE Pipe; AWWA C906.

q: Which wells are dug with earth augers, are usually under 30 m deep, range from 2 to 30 in. in diameter, and are lined with metal, vitrified tile or concrete?
n: Bored wells are made with earth augers, are usually under 30 m deep and 2–30 in. in diameter, and are lined (cased) with metal, vitrified tile or concrete. Source: US EPA Manual of Individual and Non-Public Water Supply Systems.

q: Which of the following is commonly used for water treatment (disinfection)?
n: Chlorine (as gas or hypochlorite) is the standard disinfectant for potable water, killing pathogens and leaving a residual. Source: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality; PNSDW (DOH AO 2017-0010).

q: Where is the water meter located?
o: Right after the main distribution line connection
Within the RROW, right before the property line
n: The water meter is installed within the road right-of-way (sidewalk), just before the property line, so the utility can read and service it. Source: Maynilad and Manila Water service connection standards.

q: When water travels up a vertical pipe and stops, why does it stop?
o: Gravity and friction overcome the pressure
n: Water rising in a vertical pipe stops when the pressure inside equals the outside (atmospheric plus static head) pressure, i.e. the system is in equilibrium. Source: Fluid statics; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: What is installed to cut excessive water pressure at a fixture?
n: A pressure-reducing valve (regulator) limits the downstream water pressure to protect fixtures from excessive pressure. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (excessive pressure); ASSE 1003.

q: What is the minimum supply pipe size for a tank-type water closet?
n: The minimum supply branch size for a tank-type water closet is 1/2 in. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (minimum fixture supply sizes).

q: What color identifies pipes carrying water?
n: Water lines are identified with blue (or green) pipe marking. Blue is the common color for potable water. Source: ASME A13.1 (pipe identification); Philippine plumbing practice.

q: Which material should NOT be used for a pressurized water main?
n: Ceramic (vitrified clay) pipe is brittle and made for gravity drainage, so it must not be used for pressurized water mains. Source: ASTM C700 (vitrified clay pipe); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which pipe is NOT recommended for a water line?
n: Lead leaches into drinking water and is toxic, so lead pipe is banned for water lines. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (prohibited materials); WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality.

q: What is the recommended size, in gallons, for a water tank that will serve a 2-story residence with 7 occupants?
n: At roughly 50 gallons per person per day, 7 occupants need about 350 gallons of storage. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (residential water demand).

q: Copper tubing comes in what forms?
n: Copper tubing comes rigid (hard-drawn) in straight lengths and soft (annealed) in coils. Types K and L are made in both. Source: ASTM B88 (copper water tube).

q: Which pipe is vulnerable to UV rays?
n: PVC degrades under UV: sunlight makes it brittle and discolored unless it is painted or shaded. Source: Plastics Pipe Institute; PVC manufacturer literature.

q: What is the main disadvantage of GI pipe in plumbing?
n: GI pipe's zinc coating wears away, and the steel then corrodes, scales inside and restricts flow. This is its main drawback. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which pipe is common for underground water lines because it doesn't corrode, but is brittle, has limited pressure rating and weak joints?
n: PVC does not corrode, but it is brittle, has limited pressure ratings and its solvent joints are weak points. Source: ASTM D1785 (PVC pipe); PPI handbook.

q: Which describes PPR pipes used locally for water lines?
o: Resists chemicals, corrosion and high temperatures
n: PPR resists chemicals and corrosion, handles hot water (up to about 95°C) and has fused joints, so it is widely used for hot and cold lines. Source: DIN 8077/8078 (PP-R pipes); manufacturer literature.

q: What valve in a curb box shuts off a building's water supply in emergencies, turned with a key?
n: A curb cock (curb stop) is a valve in a curb box on the service line, turned with a long key to shut off the building supply. Source: AWWA C800; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which valve lets water flow in one direction only?
n: A check valve allows flow in one direction only and blocks reverse flow. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which valve comes right after the water meter?
n: A check valve is installed right after the water meter so water cannot flow back through the meter into the public main. Source: Water utility service connection standards; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which valve controls both temperature and flow in a shower?
n: A thermostatic mixing valve blends hot and cold water to a set temperature and controls flow, preventing scalding in showers. Source: ASSE 1016/1070 (shower valves).

q: Which valve is commonly used to open, close and throttle flow in a pipeline?
n: A globe valve has a disc that seats against flow, so it is built for opening, closing and especially throttling (regulating) flow. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; MSS SP-80.
